step_title: Find the Indian Standard for your product
step_description: Search for the Indian Standard against the product using the Application/Licence-related search on MANAK Online; if it cannot be found, send a query to the concerned BIS technical department.
source_page_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Bureau of Indian Standards (Product Certification)

step_title: Submit application online on MANAK Online
step_description: BIS accepts product certification applications, including all payments, in online mode only, through the www.manakonline.in portal.
source_page_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Bureau of Indian Standards (Product Certification)

step_description: BIS carries out an assessment of the manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capability through a visit to the factory premises.
fees_info: Inspection fee: Rs. 7,000 per man-day, payable before the preliminary inspection visit
source_page_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Bureau of Indian Standards (Product Certification)

step_description: Conformity to the relevant Indian Standard is established either through third-party laboratory testing, testing in the manufacturer's own premises, or a combination of both. Under Option-2, only test reports from BIS, or a BIS-recognised/empanelled laboratory, are acceptable, and must generally not be more than 90 days old.
source_page_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Bureau of Indian Standards (Product Certification)

step_title: Licence granted and marking/annual fee deposited
step_description: After successful evaluation, the applicant deposits the annual licence fee plus the minimum marking fee specified for the product (as per Annexure I of Scheme-I of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018, as amended). The licence permits use of the ISI Standard Mark for the varieties covered under its granted scope.
fees_info: Annual licence fee: Rs. 1,000 plus product-specific minimum marking fee
source_page_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Bureau of Indian Standards (Product Certification)

step_title: Average time to grant of licence
step_description: Average time for grant of licence under Option-2 (existing acceptable test report) is generally about one month; under Option-1 (BIS-arranged testing) it is generally about four months from receipt of a complete application. Actual time may vary due to query responses, scheduling of inspection(s), sample deposition and fee payment.
processing_time: Option-2: ~1 month; Option-1: ~4 months (from date of complete application)
source_page_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Bureau of Indian Standards (Product Certification)

step_description: Certification under Scheme-I may initially be granted for up to two years and covers only the varieties mentioned in the licence. On renewal, the licence may be extended for up to five years from the last date of validity, subject to application with requisite fee and documents.
processing_time: Initial validity: up to 2 years; renewable up to 5 years
source_page_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Bureau of Indian Standards (Product Certification)

step_description: BIS carries out surprise factory surveillance inspections (through BIS officers or appointed agents) to verify continued conformity, and also carries out market surveillance by purchasing ISI-marked product samples for third-party lab testing.
source_page_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Bureau of Indian Standards (Product Certification)

step_description: A foreign manufacturer seeking an ISI mark for export to India must nominate an Authorised Indian Representative, a registered Indian entity or resident who handles communication with BIS on the manufacturer's behalf; an AIR normally represents only one foreign manufacturer.
source_page_title: About FMCS - Bureau of Indian Standards

step_description: Application, factory assessment and testing follow a process broadly similar to the domestic Scheme-I product certification route, coordinated through the AIR.
source_page_title: Grant of License - FMCS - Bureau of Indian Standards

applicant_type: Manufacturer (domestic or foreign, via AIR if applicable)
service_name: Registration for notified electronics/IT or solar products
step_title: Confirm the product is covered by a notified CRO/QCO
step_description: CRS applies only to products specifically notified under an order such as the Electronics and IT Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order, 2012, or the MNRE Solar Photovoltaics order of 2017 - not to all electronics or solar products generally.

step_title: Test at a BIS-recognised lab and apply for registration
step_description: Manufacturers must have the product tested at a BIS-recognised laboratory and then apply for registration through the CRS portal; registration is granted per manufacturer/factory location, brand and model.

Any jeweller wishing to sell hallmarked gold/silver jewellery or artefacts applies online on the BIS portal (manakonline.in). The certificate of registration is granted instantly, without needing to upload documents or pay any fee.
source_page_title: Hallmarking overview - Bureau of Indian Standards

step_title: Approach a BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC)
step_description: A consumer can get their own jewellery/sample tested at any BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking Centre, on a chargeable basis; the AHC issues an Assay Report against the identifications marked on the article.
fees_info: Chargeable (testing charge set by the AHC)
source_page_title: Hallmarking overview - Bureau of Indian Standards
